name: PA-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a +23 point Republican partisan lean
Incumbent John Joyce running with a large financial advantage ($3.8M cash vs $16K)
Prediction markets price Joyce at 97% to win
Democrat Beth Farnham has raised only $55K with no outside support
model.rationale: The district's heavy Republican lean, Joyce's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising edge, and markets pricing him at 97% all point to a safe Republican hold; Farnham's minimal resources give her no realistic path.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending for Farnham or a major scandal involving Joyce would be the only plausible source of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 13th District is a deeply Republican seat, and incumbent John Joyce is seeking another term with every structural advantage. He has raised about $2.4 million and holds nearly $3.8 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Beth Farnham has raised roughly $55,000 with no outside spending on either side. No independent polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Joyce about a 97% chance of winning, consistent with the district's strong partisan lean and the incumbent's financial dominance. The forecast expects Joyce to win comfortably, with only a remote chance of an upset absent extraordinary developments.
